title: The tenth of Muharram
hookLine: Husayn and his companions and family are killed on the day of Ashura

cards: Before Karbala, the tenth day of Muharram already had a name: Ashura.
Bukhari records that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Medina, he found the Jews of the city fasting on that day, remembering how God had saved Moses and his people.

The Prophet fasted it too, and asked his followers to fast. So it was a day of rescue, kept with a fast. Then came a morning on a plain beside the Euphrates, and the same day gained a second memory, this one of grief.

teach.b: The histories tell the morning slowly, and it is right to tell it plainly. Husayn's small band faces the army.

One man rides out from the army's ranks and crosses over: al-Hurr, the commander who first blocked Husayn's road, whose horses Husayn had watered. He asks if there is any repentance for him, and fights at Husayn's side.
Then, through the day, the companions fall one by one. Then the young men of the family: sons, nephews, brothers. Tradition counts seventy-two in all who died with him.
And at the last, Husayn himself, thirsty, is killed. The women and children are taken captive, among them his sister Zaynab, and his son Ali, who was too sick to fight.

teach.h: SUNNI AND SHIA BOTH HONOR HIM.
teach.b: Sunni and Shia Muslims both honor Husayn. Sunni Muslims honor him as the Prophet's grandson, and Sunni practice keeps the Ashura fast from the Prophet's own example.
For Shia Muslims, Husayn is the third Imam, and the tenth is the center of the year's mourning: gatherings, elegies, tears, the story told again so that it is never told for the last time.
The Qur'an speaks to those who fall in God's way.
In Pickthall's translation: "And call not those who are slain in the way of Allah 'dead.' Nay, they are living, only ye perceive not."
Shia tradition reads Karbala in the light of that verse. One date carries two memories, a people rescued and a family falling, and both are kept.

how: On the tenth of Muharram, Shia Muslims gather to mourn Husayn with elegies and recitations of Karbala; Sunni Muslims honor him too, and Sunni communities keep the Ashura fast that the Prophet kept.

games.q: the tenth of Muharram — tap the pairs.
p: too sick to fight, taken captive

s: Ashura only began to be marked after Karbala
Bukhari records the Prophet fasting on it in Medina, for Moses' rescue.
al-Hurr, who first blocked Husayn's road, fought beside him on the last day
the histories say he crossed over and asked if there was repentance for him.
Sunni Muslims honor him as the Prophet's grandson; for Shia Muslims he is also the third Imam.

games.q: you're al-Hurr. you blocked Husayn's road, and now you're in the army facing him on the tenth. what do you do?
o: stay in the ranks and follow orders.
games.why: the histories say he rode over, asked whether there was repentance for him, and fought at Husayn's side.

practice: There's nothing to fix in this one. Let the names you heard come and go, al-Hurr, al-Abbas, Zaynab, Husayn, and keep them company a while, the way people sit with a family after a death.
If you pray, you can say, as the Qur'an teaches, we are Allah's and unto Him we are returning; if you don't, just keep the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Ashura. The tenth day of Muharram: the day the Prophet fasted for Moses' rescue, and the day Husayn and his companions were killed at Karbala. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Ashura, the name of the tenth day of the month of Muharram.

carryVoice: Your line: the tenth day. Rest gently with it, and with all of them. Until tomorrow.
